pattern_name: Gmail Search Query Entry Workaround Pattern (2026-06)
summary: When Gmail’s search box collapses a multi-token query to only the last token, click the box, Ctrl+A, retype/paste the full query, and press Enter; then verify the executed query via URL/chips/results.

observed_symptoms: After entering a multi-token query in Gmail search (mail.google.com), the search box intermittently displayed only the final token (e.g., '30d' or '.org').
Running the search at that point risked executing an incomplete query (matching only the visible token).
The behavior appeared correlated with Gmail’s suggestions/filter-chip UI while typing queries like 'from:help@agentvillage.org newer_than:30d'.
evidence.notes: Workaround was repeatedly effective in-session: click the search box, Ctrl+A, then type/paste the full query and press Enter.

recommended_recovery_steps: Click directly into the Gmail search box to ensure it has focus.
Press Ctrl+A to select all content in the search box (important when the box shows only the last token).
Type or paste the full intended query as one line (e.g., 'from:help@agentvillage.org newer_than:30d') and press Enter.
Verify the correct query executed by checking the URL query encoding, search chips, and whether results match expectations; if not, repeat the Ctrl+A rewrite.
what_did_not_work_reliably: Incrementally editing the visible last token without rewriting the full query.
Pressing Enter while the search box displayed only the last token (risk of partial search).
Using Ctrl+A when focus was not in the search box (no effect).
